title: Keep the Garden Display Focused
scenario: A community garden kiosk displays details for one plant selected by a volunteer. The selected plant remains owned by the volunteer's garden record, while GardenDisplay only observes it for as long as the kiosk screen is open.
problem_statement: `GardenDisplay::highlight` is called when a volunteer selects a `Plant`, but the display currently reports that no plant is focused. Correct `GardenDisplay::highlight` so that `GardenDisplay` observes the selected live plant. If the volunteer later renames that same plant, `focusedLabel()` must show the new label without selecting it again.
constraints: Do not change the public methods of `Plant` or `GardenDisplay`.
The selected `Plant` remains alive while the display uses it.
`GardenDisplay` observes only one selected plant at a time.
learning_objective: Use a raw non-owning pointer to store the identity of an existing live object and access that pointee safely through a null-aware public query.
instructions: Update the implementation of `GardenDisplay::highlight`. Keep the existing behavior of `hasFocus()` and `focusedLabel()` intact.
expected_concepts: binding a pointer to an existing object
hints: The display should retain the selected plant itself, not just decide whether a focus exists.
Look at the type of `focused_` and the object received by `highlight`.
The label returned after a later rename should come from the originally selected `Plant`.
explanation: `GardenDisplay` needs to retain the identity of the existing `Plant` passed to `highlight`. Storing that plant's address in `focused_` makes `focusedLabel()` read the current label from the same live object. The existing null check continues to handle a display that has not selected anything yet.
learner_goal: Make the garden display continue showing the selected plant's current label after that plant is renamed elsewhere.
